title.zh: 卷九十四 列傳第三十二: 夾谷清臣 襄 夾谷衡 完顏安國 瑤里孛迭
title.en: Volume 94 Biographies 32: Jiaguqingchen, Xiang, Jia Guheng, Wan Yananguo, Yaolibeidie
title.raw: 卷九十四 列傳第三十二: 夾谷清臣 襄 夾谷衡 完顏安國 瑤里孛迭 Volume 94 Biographies 32: Jiaguqingchen, Xiang, Jia Guheng, Wan Yananguo, Yaolibeidie

sentences.zh: 夾谷清臣

translations.literal: Jiagu Qingchen
translations.idiomatic: Jiagu Qingchen

sentences.zh: 夾谷清臣，本名阿不沙，胡里改路桓篤人也。

translations.literal: Jiagu Qingchen, original name A'busha, was a man of Huandu in the Huligai Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Jiagu Qingchen, whose original name was A'busha, came from Huandu in the Huligai Circuit.

sentences.zh: 姿狀雄偉，善騎謝。

translations.literal: His bearing was imposing and he was skilled at riding and archery.
translations.idiomatic: He had a commanding physique and excelled at mounted archery.

sentences.zh: 皇統八年，襲祖駁達猛安。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Huangtong, he inherited his grandfather's Bodafa meng'an post.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Huangtong (1148), he succeeded to his grandfather's hereditary meng'an at Bodafa.

sentences.zh: 大定元年，聞世宗即位，率本部軍六千赴中都會之，以功遷昭武大將軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dading, hearing that Shizong had ascended the throne, he led six thousand troops of his command to Zhongdu to join him and, for his merit, was promoted to Zhaowu Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong took the throne in the first year of Dading (1161), Qingchen led six thousand men of his unit to Zhongdu to rally to him and was promoted to Zhaowu Grand General for his service.

sentences.zh: 從右副元帥紇石烈志甯為管押萬戶，接應左都監完顏思敬，逐窩斡餘黨，敗之柔遠，至抹拔里達悉獲之。

translations.literal: Following the Right Deputy Commander-in-Chief Heshilie Zhining as supervising commander of ten thousand households, he supported the Left Chief Inspector Wanyan Sijing in pursuing the remnant band of Wohe, defeated them at Rouyuan, and pursued them to Mobali, capturing them all.
translations.idiomatic: He served under the Right Deputy Commander-in-Chief Heshilie Zhining as supervising commander of ten thousand households, joined the Left Chief Inspector Wanyan Sijing in hunting down Wohe's remaining followers, routed them at Rouyuan, and ran them down to Mobali, where the entire force was taken.

sentences.zh: 賊平，遷鎮國上將軍，知潁順軍事。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified, he was transferred to Zhenguo Grand General and made responsible for Yingshun military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion was crushed, he was promoted to Zhenguo Grand General and put in charge of military affairs at Yingshun.

sentences.zh: 會宋兵二萬襲陷汝州，殺刺史烏古孫麻發及漢軍二千。

translations.literal: It happened that twenty thousand Song troops raided and seized Ruzhou, killing the prefect Wugusun Mafa and two thousand Han troops.
translations.idiomatic: Song forces numbering twenty thousand then stormed and captured Ruzhou, killing the prefect Wugusun Mafa along with two thousand Han soldiers.

sentences.zh: 河南統軍宗尹遣萬戶孛術魯定方與清臣等領騎兵四千往擊之。

translations.literal: The Henan Commander-in-Chief Zong Yin sent the commander of ten thousand households Pusulu Dingfang with Qingchen and others to lead four thousand cavalry to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: The Henan Commander-in-Chief Zong Yin dispatched Pusulu Dingfang, commander of ten thousand households, together with Qingchen and others at the head of four thousand horsemen to attack them.

sentences.zh: 宋人棄城遁，遂複汝州。

translations.literal: The Song men abandoned the city and fled, and Ruzhou was thereby recovered.
translations.idiomatic: The Song troops abandoned the city and fled, and Ruzhou was retaken.

sentences.zh: 三年五月，從志寧複取宿州，宋將李世輔大敗遁去，志寧複遣清臣等以兵追襲，又敗之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the third year, following Zhining he recovered Suzhou; the Song general Li Shipu was greatly defeated and fled; Zhining again sent Qingchen and others with troops to pursue and strike them, and defeated them again.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the third year (1163), he followed Zhining in retaking Suzhou. After the Song general Li Shipu was routed and fled, Zhining sent Qingchen and others in pursuit, and they defeated the enemy again.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，授宿州防禦使。

translations.literal: When news of the victory arrived, he was appointed Defender of Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On report of the victory, he was appointed Defender of Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 移博州，改西北路招討都監，遷烏古十壘部族節度使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Bozhou, changed to Northwest Circuit Pacification Commissioner, and promoted to Commissioner of the Wugu Shilei Tribal Command.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to Bozhou, made Northwest Circuit Pacification Commissioner, and then promoted to Commissioner of the Wugu Shilei tribal command.

sentences.zh: 十二年，授右副都點檢，遷左副都點檢，出為陝西路統軍使，兼知京兆府事。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was appointed Right Deputy Chief Inspector, transferred to Left Deputy Chief Inspector, and sent out as Shaanxi Circuit Commander-in-Chief, concurrently administering Jingzhao Prefecture affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year (1172) he was made Right Deputy Chief Inspector, then Left Deputy Chief Inspector, and sent out as Commander-in-Chief of the Shaanxi Circuit while also serving as administrator of Jingzhao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 朝辭，賜以金帶廄馬，仍諭之曰：「卿典禁兵，日侍左右，勤勞久矣，故以是授卿，宜益思勉。

translations.literal: At his court farewell he was granted a gold belt and stable horses, and was further instructed: "You have long commanded the forbidden troops and attended at my side day after day with devoted labor; therefore this is conferred on you—you should strive all the more."
translations.idiomatic: When he took leave at court, the emperor bestowed a gold belt and imperial horses and told him: "You have long commanded the palace guard and attended me daily with tireless service; that is why I am sending you out—do not slacken your efforts."

sentences.zh: 」二十六年，改西京留守。

translations.literal: " In the twenty-sixth year he was changed to Western Capital Garrison Commander.
translations.idiomatic: " In the twenty-sixth year (1186) he was appointed Garrison Commander of the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 閱三歲，遷樞密副使。

translations.literal: After three years he was transferred to Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later he was promoted to Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 明昌元年，初議出師，以本職充東北路兵馬都統制使，既而詔止之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Mingchang, when an expedition was first discussed, he was appointed in his present office as Commander-in-Chief of Northeast Circuit forces, but shortly an edict halted it.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Mingchang (1190), when a campaign was first proposed, he was named Commander-in-Chief of Northeast Circuit forces in his current post, but an edict soon called the expedition off.

sentences.zh: 俄以其女為昭儀，眷倚益重。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward his daughter was made Lady of Brilliant Comportment, and imperial favor toward him grew heavier.
translations.idiomatic: Before long his daughter was made a zhaoyi (imperial consort), and the emperor's reliance on him deepened.

sentences.zh: 二年，拜尚書左丞。

translations.literal: In the second year he was appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year (1191) he was appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 頃之，進平章政事，封芮國公，賜同本朝人。

translations.literal: Before long he was advanced to Grand Councilor, enfeoffed as Duke of Rui, and granted status equal to native Jin subjects.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was promoted to Grand Councilor, enfeoffed as Duke of Rui, and granted the privileges of a native Jin subject.

sentences.zh: 四年，遷右丞相，監修國史。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was transferred to Right Chancellor and made supervisor of the compilation of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year (1193) he became Right Chancellor and was put in charge of compiling the national history.

sentences.zh: 時議簽軍戍邊，上問：「漢人與夏人孰勇？

translations.literal: At the time there was discussion of drafting troops to garrison the frontier; the emperor asked: "Between Han men and Tangut men, which are braver?"
translations.idiomatic: When the court debated drafting troops for frontier garrison duty, the emperor asked: "Which are braver—Han soldiers or Tangut soldiers?"

sentences.zh: 」清臣曰：「漢人勇。

translations.literal: " Qingchen said: "Han men are brave."
translations.idiomatic: " Qingchen replied: "The Han are braver."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「昔元昊擾邊，宋終不能制，何也？

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "In the past Yuanhao harassed the border and Song could never control him—why?"
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said: "When Yuanhao once raided the frontier, Song could never bring him to heel—why was that?"

sentences.zh: 」清臣曰：「宋馭軍法不可得知，今西南路人殊勝彼也。

translations.literal: " Qingchen said: "Song's methods of controlling troops cannot be known; the men of our Southwest Circuit today are far superior to them."
translations.idiomatic: " Qingchen said: "One cannot know how Song controlled its armies, but the troops of our Southwest Circuit today are far better than theirs were."

sentences.zh: 」未幾，遷崇進，改封戴。

translations.literal: " Before long he was promoted to Honored Advancement and his fief was changed to Dai.
translations.idiomatic: " Shortly afterward he was promoted to Honored Advancement and his title was changed to Duke of Dai.

sentences.zh: 一日，上謂宰臣曰：「人有以《八陣圖》來上者，其圖果何如？

translations.literal: One day the emperor said to the chief ministers: "Someone has presented the Eight-Array Diagram to the throne—what is that diagram really like?"
translations.idiomatic: One day the emperor told his chief ministers: "Someone has submitted the Eight-Array Diagram—what is it really good for?"

sentences.zh: 朕嘗觀宋白所集《武經》，然其載攻守之法亦多難行。

translations.literal: I have looked at the Military Canon compiled by Song Bai, yet many of the attack-and-defense methods it records are hard to carry out.
translations.idiomatic: I have read the Military Canon compiled by Song Bai, but many of the offensive and defensive methods it records are impractical.

sentences.zh: 」清臣曰：「兵書皆定法，難以應變。

translations.literal: " Qingchen said: "Military books are all fixed methods and are hard to apply to changing circumstances."
translations.idiomatic: " Qingchen said: "Military manuals lay down fixed methods and cannot adapt to changing circumstances."

sentences.zh: 本朝行兵之術，惟用正奇二軍，臨敵制變，以正為奇，以奇為正，故無往不克。

translations.literal: Our dynasty's art of campaigning uses only the two forces, regular and extraordinary; facing the enemy one shapes changes, making regular into extraordinary and extraordinary into regular, and therefore there is nowhere it does not conquer.
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty's way of war relies solely on the regular and extraordinary forces: facing the enemy, one improvises—turning the regular into the extraordinary and the extraordinary into the regular—so that no engagement goes unconquered.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「自古用兵亦不出奇正二法耳。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Since antiquity campaigning has not gone beyond the two methods of regular and extraordinary."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said: "Since antiquity, warfare has never gone beyond the pairing of regular and extraordinary forces."

sentences.zh: 且學古兵法如學弈棋，未能自得於心，而欲用舊陣勢以接敵，亦以疏矣。」

translations.literal: Moreover, studying ancient military methods is like learning to play chess: if one has not mastered it in one's own mind yet wishes to use old formations to meet the enemy, that is also quite crude."
translations.idiomatic: Besides, studying ancient tactics is like learning chess: if you have not internalized them and yet try to meet the enemy with old formations, you are being quite naive."

sentences.zh: 尋上表丐閑，不許。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he submitted a memorial requesting leisure and was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He soon memorialized asking to be relieved of duty, but the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 固請，乃賜告省親，諭之曰：「聞卿母老，欲令歸省，故特給假五十日，馳驛以往，至彼可為一月留也。

translations.literal: He pressed his request firmly; then he was granted leave to visit his family and was instructed: "I have heard your mother is old and wish to let you return to visit her; therefore I specially grant fifty days' leave—go by express relay; once there you may stay a month."
translations.idiomatic: When he pressed the matter, he was granted leave to visit his family. The emperor told him: "I hear your mother is elderly and wish you to go home to see her, so I am granting you fifty days—travel by express relay; you may remain there for a month."

sentences.zh: 」五年二月，上禦凝和殿，清臣省覲還，謁上。

translations.literal: " In the second month of the fifth year the emperor held court at the Ninghe Hall; Qingchen, returned from his family visit, paid his respects.
translations.idiomatic: " In the second month of the fifth year (1194), the emperor held audience at the Ninghe Hall. Qingchen, back from his visit home, came to pay his respects.

sentences.zh: 上問：「卿母健否？

translations.literal: The emperor asked: "Is your mother in good health?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked: "Is your mother in good health?"

sentences.zh: 其壽幾何？

translations.literal: How old is she?
translations.idiomatic: How old is she?

sentences.zh: 相別幾年矣？

translations.literal: How many years have you been apart?
translations.idiomatic: How many years have you been apart?

sentences.zh: 」清臣對曰：「臣母年八十三矣，別十年，幸頗強健。

translations.literal: " Qingchen replied: "My mother is eighty-three; we have been apart ten years, and fortunately she is still quite vigorous."
translations.idiomatic: " Qingchen answered: "My mother is eighty-three. We have been apart ten years, but fortunately she is still quite hale."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「何不來此？

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Why does she not come here?"
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor asked: "Why does she not come here?"

sentences.zh: 」曰：「急於家務，故不欲離耳。

translations.literal: " He said: "She is busy with household affairs and therefore does not wish to leave."
translations.idiomatic: " He said: "She is absorbed in household affairs and does not want to leave home."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「老人多如是，所謂'血氣既衰，戒之在得'也。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "The old are often like this—it is what is called 'when the blood and breath have declined, the warning lies in grasping gain.'"
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said: "The elderly are often like that—it is what the saying means: 'When vigor has waned, beware of clinging to gain.'"

sentences.zh: 」複謂清臣：「胡里改路風俗何如？

translations.literal: " He again said to Qingchen: "How are the customs of the Huligai Circuit?"
translations.idiomatic: " He then asked Qingchen: "How are customs in the Huligai Circuit nowadays?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「視舊則稍知禮貌，而勇勁不及矣。

translations.literal: " He replied: "Compared with old times they know ritual and decorum somewhat better, but their bold vigor no longer measures up."
translations.idiomatic: " He answered: "Compared with the old days they are somewhat more observant of ritual, but their martial spirit no longer matches what it was."

sentences.zh: 」因言西南、西北等路軍人，其閑習弓矢，亦非複曩時。

translations.literal: " He went on to say that soldiers of the Southwest, Northwest, and other circuits, in their leisure practice of bow and arrow, likewise were no longer as in former times.
translations.idiomatic: " He added that soldiers on the Southwest, Northwest, and other circuits no longer practiced archery in their spare time as they once had.

sentences.zh: 六年，遷儀同三司，進拜左丞相，改封密。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to Honorary Three Excellencies, advanced to Left Chancellor, and his fief was changed to Mi.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year (1195) he was promoted to Honorary Three Excellencies and Left Chancellor, and his title was changed to Duke of Mi.

sentences.zh: 受命出師，行尚書省事於臨潢府。

translations.literal: Receiving orders to take the field, he exercised the duties of the Department of State Affairs at Linhuang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to take command in the field, he conducted the affairs of the Department of State Affairs from Linhuang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 清臣遣人偵知虛實，以輕騎八千，令宣徽使移剌敏為都統，左衛將軍充、招討使完顏安國為左右翼，分領前隊，自選精兵一萬以當後隊。

translations.literal: Qingchen sent men to scout and learn the true situation; with eight thousand light cavalry he appointed the Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat Yila Min as commander-in-chief, the Left Guard General Chong and the Pacification Commissioner Wanyan Anguo as left and right wings to lead the vanguard in division, and himself selected ten thousand elite troops to serve as the rear.
translations.idiomatic: Qingchen sent scouts to learn the enemy's strength, then advanced with eight thousand light cavalry. He made Palace Secretariat Commissioner Yila Min overall commander, with Left Guard General Chong and Pacification Commissioner Wanyan Anguo leading the left and right wings of the vanguard, while he personally chose ten thousand elite troops for the rear guard.

sentences.zh: 進至合勒河，前隊敏等於栲栳濼攻營十四，下之，回迎大軍，屬部斜出掩其所獲羊馬資物以歸。

translations.literal: Advancing to the Helle River, the vanguard under Min and others at Kaoluo Marsh attacked fourteen camps and took them, then turned back to meet the main army; subordinate units slipped away on the flank to cover and carry off the sheep, horses, and supplies they had seized.
translations.idiomatic: They advanced to the Helle River, where Min's vanguard stormed fourteen camps at Kaoluo Marsh and took them, then turned back to join the main force. Subordinate units broke away on the flank to seize and drive off the captured sheep, horses, and supplies.

sentences.zh: 清臣遣人責其賧罰，北阻珝由此叛去，大侵掠。

translations.literal: Qingchen sent men to impose fines and penalties on them; Beizu Xu thereby rebelled and fled, launching great raids.
translations.idiomatic: Qingchen sent officers to impose fines on them for this; Beizu Xu thereupon rebelled and fled, launching widespread raids.

sentences.zh: 上遣責清臣，命右丞相襄代之。

translations.literal: The emperor sent envoys to rebuke Qingchen and ordered the Right Chancellor Xiang to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent envoys to rebuke Qingchen and ordered Right Chancellor Xiang to replace him.

sentences.zh: 承安五年，降授橫海軍節度使兼滄州管內觀察使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Cheng'an he was demoted and appointed Military Commissioner of the Henghai Army and Concurrent Observation Commissioner within Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Cheng'an (1200) he was demoted to Military Commissioner of the Henghai Army and Concurrent Observation Commissioner of Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，上諭宰臣曰：「清臣舊有勞效，罪狀未甚明，若降授，應須告致仕耳。

translations.literal: Earlier the emperor had instructed the chief ministers: "Qingchen formerly had meritorious service; his offenses are not very clear—if he is demoted, he ought simply to be told to retire."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the emperor had told his chief ministers: "Qingchen has past service to his credit, and his offenses are not altogether clear—if we demote him, we ought simply to let him retire."

sentences.zh: 」初擬知廣寧府，上曰：「姑與滄州。

translations.literal: " At first it was proposed that he administer Guangning Prefecture; the emperor said: "For the time being give him Cangzhou."
translations.idiomatic: " At first the court proposed making him prefect of Guangning; the emperor said: "For now give him Cangzhou."

sentences.zh: 」既而又曰：「與則與之，第恐有人言也。

translations.literal: " Then he said again: "Give it if we give it—only I fear there will be talk."
translations.idiomatic: " Then he added: "Give it if we must—but I fear people will talk."

sentences.zh: 」尋複致仕。

translations.literal: " Before long he was again retired.
translations.idiomatic: " Before long he was allowed to retire again.

sentences.zh: 泰和二年薨，年七十。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taihe he died; he was seventy.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Taihe (1202), at the age of seventy.

sentences.zh: 子麼查剌襲猛安。

translations.literal: His son Machala inherited the meng'an.
translations.idiomatic: His son Machala inherited the meng'an post.

sentences.zh: 初議征討，清臣主其事，既而領軍出征，雖屢獲捷，而貪小利，遂致北邊不寧者數歲，天下尤之。

translations.literal: When the expedition was first discussed Qingchen directed the affair; afterward he led the army into the field and, though he won victories repeatedly, through greed for small gains he caused the northern frontier to be unsettled for several years, and all under Heaven blamed him.
translations.idiomatic: When the northern campaign was first proposed, Qingchen took charge; he then led the army in person and, though he won repeated victories, his greed for petty booty left the northern frontier troubled for years, and public opinion blamed him heavily.

sentences.zh: 內族 襄

translations.literal: Inner Clan: Xiang
translations.idiomatic: Inner Clan: Xiang

sentences.zh: 丞相襄，本名唵，昭祖五世孫也。

translations.literal: Chancellor Xiang, original name An, was a fifth-generation descendant of Zhaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Xiang, whose original name was An, was a fifth-generation descendant of Zhaozu.

sentences.zh: 祖什古乃從太祖平遼，以功授上京世襲猛安，曆東京留守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shigunai followed Taizu in pacifying Liao and, for his merit, was granted the hereditary meng'an of Shangjing; he served as Garrison Commander of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shigunai followed Taizu in the conquest of Liao and, for his service, received the hereditary meng'an of Shangjing; he later served as Garrison Commander of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 父阿魯帶，皇統初北伐有功，拜參知政事。

translations.literal: His father Aludai, at the beginning of Huangtong, had merit in the northern campaign and was appointed Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: His father Aludai distinguished himself in the northern campaigns at the start of Huangtong and was appointed Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 襄幼有志節，善騎射，多勇略，年十八襲世爵。

translations.literal: Xiang in youth had resolve and integrity, was skilled at riding and archery, and possessed much bold strategy; at eighteen he inherited the hereditary rank.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Xiang showed purpose and integrity, excelled at mounted archery, and possessed bold strategic talent; at eighteen he inherited the family rank.

sentences.zh: 大定初，契丹叛，從左副元帥謀衍以本部兵討賊，戰於肇州之長濼。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dading the Khitan rebelled; following the Left Deputy Commander-in-Chief Mouyan he led his command's troops to suppress the rebels and fought at Changpo in Zhaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Dading era, when the Khitan rose in revolt, Xiang followed the Left Deputy Commander-in-Chief Mouyan with his unit to suppress them and fought at Changpo in Zhaozhou.

sentences.zh: 襄先登鏖擊，足中流矢，裹創以戰，氣愈厲，七戰皆勝。

translations.literal: Xiang was first to ascend and fought fiercely in close combat; an arrow struck his foot, yet he bound the wound and continued fighting, his spirit growing fiercer; in seven engagements he was victorious every time.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang led the charge into fierce hand-to-hand fighting. An arrow struck his foot, but he bound the wound and kept fighting with growing ferocity, winning all seven engagements.

sentences.zh: 謀衍握其手曰：「今日之捷，皆公力也。

translations.literal: Mouyan grasped his hand and said: "Today's victory is entirely your doing."
translations.idiomatic: Mouyan took his hand and said: "Today's victory is entirely your doing."

sentences.zh: 」賊走渡霿𩃭河，追及之。

translations.literal: " The rebels fled across the Mo River and were overtaken.
translations.idiomatic: " The rebels fled across the Mo River, and he overtook them.

sentences.zh: 所駐地多草，賊乘風縱火，襄亦縱火，立空地以俟。

translations.literal: The place where they were stationed had much grass; the rebels took advantage of the wind to set fires, and Xiang also set fires and stood on open ground to wait.
translations.idiomatic: Their camp stood in tall grass. The rebels set fires downwind, but Xiang did the same and held his men on open ground to wait.

sentences.zh: 戰十餘合，賊益困。

translations.literal: They fought more than ten rounds and the rebels grew ever more distressed.
translations.idiomatic: After more than ten clashes the rebels were increasingly hard pressed.

sentences.zh: 襄謂謀衍曰：「今不乘此平殄，後將有悔。

translations.literal: Xiang said to Mouyan: "If we do not take this chance to destroy them completely, we will regret it later."
translations.idiomatic: Xiang told Mouyan: "If we do not annihilate them now, we will regret it later."

sentences.zh: 」謀衍然之。

translations.literal: " Mouyan agreed.
translations.idiomatic: " Mouyan agreed.

sentences.zh: 襄率眾搏戰。

translations.literal: Xiang led the troops in fierce combat.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang led his men into a pitched battle.

sentences.zh: 大敗之，俘獲萬計。

translations.literal: He inflicted a great defeat on them; captives and booty numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: He routed them utterly, taking prisoners and booty by the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 會朝廷遣平章政事僕散忠義代謀衍將，襄複從忠義追賊至嫋嶺西之陷泉，及之，率右翼身先奮擊，賊大潰，人馬相蹂而死，陷泉幾平。

translations.literal: It happened that the court sent the Grand Councilor Pusans Zhongyi to replace Mouyan as commander; Xiang again followed Zhongyi in pursuing the rebels to Xianquan west of Niaoling, overtook them, led the right wing and charged ahead in person; the rebels were greatly routed, men and horses trampling one another to death; Xianquan was nearly pacified.
translations.idiomatic: When the court sent Grand Councilor Pusans Zhongyi to replace Mouyan in command, Xiang again followed Zhongyi in pursuit to Xianquan west of Niaoling. He overtook the enemy, led the right wing in a personal charge, and routed them so completely that men and horses trampled one another to death; Xianquan was nearly cleared.

sentences.zh: 賊酉窩斡僅與數十騎遁去，卒就擒，論功為第一。

translations.literal: The rebel leader Wohe escaped with only several dozen horsemen, but was finally captured; in reckoning merit he was ranked first.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel leader Wohe escaped with only a few dozen horsemen but was eventually captured; Xiang was ranked first in merit.

sentences.zh: 有司擬淄州刺史，詔特授亳州防禦使，時年二十三。

translations.literal: The responsible offices proposed him as prefect of Zizhou; an edict specially appointed him Defender of Bozhou; he was then twenty-three.
translations.idiomatic: The personnel office proposed him for prefect of Zizhou, but an edict specially appointed him Defender of Bozhou when he was twenty-three.

sentences.zh: 宋人犯南鄙，襄為潁、壽都統，率甲士二千人渡潁水，敗敵兵五千，複潁州，生擒宋帥楊思。

translations.literal: Song men violated the southern frontier; Xiang was commander of Ying and Shou, led two thousand armored soldiers across the Ying River, defeated five thousand enemy troops, recovered Yingzhou, and captured alive the Song commander Yang Si.
translations.idiomatic: When Song forces invaded the southern frontier, Xiang, as commander of Ying and Shou, led two thousand armored troops across the Ying River, defeated five thousand enemy soldiers, retook Yingzhou, and captured the Song commander Yang Si alive.

sentences.zh: 次濠州，宋將郭太尉退保橫澗山，襄攻之，伏弩射中其膝，督攻愈急，拔之，獲郭太尉。

translations.literal: Next at Haozhou the Song general the Grand Commandant Guo withdrew to defend Hengjian Mountain; Xiang attacked him; concealed crossbows struck his knee; he pressed the assault all the more urgently, took the position, and captured the Grand Commandant Guo.
translations.idiomatic: At Haozhou the Song general Guo the Grand Commandant fell back to Hengjian Mountain. Xiang besieged him; a hidden crossbow bolt struck Guo's knee, but Xiang pressed the assault harder, took the position, and captured Guo.

sentences.zh: 既而趨滁州，襄為先鋒，將至清流關，得宋偵者，知敵欲三道夜出，掩我不備。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he hastened to Chuzhou; Xiang served as vanguard; when about to reach Qingliu Pass he obtained a Song scout and learned the enemy intended to come out by three routes at night and strike them unawares.
translations.idiomatic: He then pressed on toward Chuzhou as vanguard. Near Qingliu Pass he captured a Song scout and learned the enemy planned a three-pronged night attack to catch them off guard.

sentences.zh: 左副元帥紇石烈志甯問計。

translations.literal: The Left Deputy Commander-in-Chief Heshilie Zhining asked his plan.
translations.idiomatic: The Left Deputy Commander-in-Chief Heshilie Zhining asked his advice.

sentences.zh: 襄曰：「今兵少地隘，儻不得關，敵至，我無所據，必先取之。

translations.literal: Xiang said: "Now our troops are few and the ground narrow; if we do not hold the pass, when the enemy arrives we will have nowhere to stand—we must seize it first."
translations.idiomatic: Xiang said: "We are few in number and the terrain is tight. If we do not hold the pass, we will have nowhere to stand when the enemy arrives—we must take it first."

sentences.zh: 」曰：「我與若孰往？

translations.literal: " He said: "Between you and me, which of us should go?"
translations.idiomatic: " Zhining asked: "Which of us should go?"

sentences.zh: 」襄曰：「元帥國家大臣，詎宜輕動？

translations.literal: " Xiang said: "The commander-in-chief is a great minister of state—how could he move lightly?"
translations.idiomatic: " Xiang said: "You are a senior minister of state—how could you risk yourself?"

sentences.zh: 襄當為公往取。

translations.literal: Xiang ought to go for you and take it.
translations.idiomatic: I should go in your place and take it.

sentences.zh: 」志寧韙之。

translations.literal: " Zhining approved.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhining agreed.

sentences.zh: 襄率騎二千，分二道，一由沖路，自以千兵間道潛登。

translations.literal: Xiang led two thousand cavalry, divided into two routes; one went by the main road while he himself with a thousand men by a hidden path stole up in secret.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang led two thousand horsemen in two columns: one along the main road, while he himself took a thousand men by a hidden path to climb the pass unseen.

sentences.zh: 既近，敵始覺。

translations.literal: When they were already near, the enemy only then became aware.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy only realized what was happening when he was already upon them.

sentences.zh: 襄攻克之，據其關，志寧履行戰地，顧謂曰：「克敵於不可勝之地，真天下英傑也。

translations.literal: Xiang stormed and took it and held the pass; Zhining walked over the battlefield and, turning to him, said: "To defeat the enemy in a place where victory seemed impossible—truly a hero of the realm."
translations.idiomatic: Xiang stormed the pass and held it. Zhining walked the battlefield and said to him: "To defeat the enemy where victory seemed impossible—truly you are a hero of the age."

sentences.zh: 」及宋乞盟，班師，召為拱衛直都指揮使，改殿前右衛將軍，轉左衛，出為東北路招討都監，遷速頻路節度使，移曷懶路兵馬都總管。

translations.literal: " When Song begged for peace the army withdrew; he was summoned as Commander of the Archway Guard Direct; changed to Right Guard General of the Hall Army; transferred to the Left Guard; sent out as Northeast Circuit Pacification Commissioner; promoted to Commissioner of the Supin Circuit; transferred to Commander-in-Chief of Yilan Circuit forces.
translations.idiomatic: " When Song sued for peace and the army withdrew, he was summoned as Commander of the Archway Guard Direct, made Right Guard General of the Hall Army, then Left Guard General, sent out as Northeast Circuit Pacification Commissioner, promoted to Commissioner of the Supin Circuit, and finally transferred to Commander-in-Chief of Yilan Circuit forces.

sentences.zh: 左丞相志甯疾甚，世宗臨問之，志寧薦襄「智勇兼濟，有經世才，他人莫及，異時任用，殆勝於臣」。

translations.literal: Left Chancellor Zhining was gravely ill; Shizong visited him in person to inquire; Zhining recommended Xiang: "Combining wisdom and courage, possessing talent to order the age—no one else can match him; employed in future he would likely surpass me."
translations.idiomatic: When Left Chancellor Zhining fell gravely ill, Shizong visited him in person. Zhining recommended Xiang: "He combines wisdom and courage and has the talent to govern an age; no one else equals him, and if employed later he would likely surpass me."

sentences.zh: 即召授殿前左副都點檢。

translations.literal: He was immediately summoned and appointed Left Deputy Chief Inspector of the Hall Army.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang was immediately summoned and appointed Left Deputy Chief Inspector of the Hall Army.

sentences.zh: 為宋生日使，宋方祈免親接國書，襄至，宋人屢來議，皆折之，迄成禮而還。

translations.literal: He served as envoy for Song's birthday; Song was then petitioning to be excused from receiving the state letter in person; when Xiang arrived, Song men came repeatedly to negotiate and he refuted them all, until the rites were completed and he returned.
translations.idiomatic: As envoy for the Song emperor's birthday, when Song was petitioning to be excused from receiving the state letter in person, Xiang went. The Song side negotiated repeatedly, but he rebutted every proposal until the ceremony was completed and he returned.

sentences.zh: 授陝西路統軍使，賜之尚服、廄馬、鞍勒、佩刀。

translations.literal: He was appointed Shaanxi Circuit Commander-in-Chief and granted court robes, stable horses, saddle and bridle, and a waist sword.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Commander-in-Chief of the Shaanxi Circuit and granted court robes, imperial horses, saddle and bridle, and a ceremonial sword.

sentences.zh: 改河南統軍使。

translations.literal: He was changed to Henan Circuit Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Commander-in-Chief of the Henan Circuit.

sentences.zh: 入為吏部尚書，轉都點檢，賜錢千萬。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Director of the Ministry of Personnel, was transferred to Chief Inspector, and was granted ten million in cash.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as Director of the Ministry of Personnel, then promoted to Chief Inspector and granted ten million in cash.

sentences.zh: 世宗謂宰執曰：「襄為人甚蘊藉，非直日，亦入宮規畫諸事，事有所付乃退，其公勤如此。

translations.literal: Shizong said to the chief administrators: "Xiang's character is very restrained; even on days when he is not on duty he enters the palace to plan various affairs and withdraws only when matters are entrusted—his public diligence is like this."
translations.idiomatic: Shizong told his chief administrators: "Xiang is deeply self-possessed. Even on days when he is not on duty he comes to the palace to discuss affairs and leaves only after matters are settled—such is his public diligence."

sentences.zh: 若襄之才豈多得哉！

translations.literal: Talents like Xiang's—how could one obtain many!
translations.idiomatic: How rarely one finds talent like Xiang's!

sentences.zh: 」擢御史大夫。

translations.literal: " He was promoted to Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: " He was promoted to Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 逾月，拜尚書右丞，諭之曰：「卿在河南經制邊事，甚有統紀，及在吏部，至為點檢，尤奉公守法，朕甚嘉之。

translations.literal: After more than a month, he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and was addressed thus: "When you managed border affairs in Henan, you maintained excellent discipline; when you served in the Ministry of Personnel and later as Chief Inspector, you were especially devoted to public duty and observant of the law. I greatly commend this.
translations.idiomatic: A month later he was made Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs. The emperor told him, "In Henan you kept border affairs in good order; in the Ministry of Personnel and as Chief Inspector you were scrupulously fair and law-abiding. I am deeply pleased with your service.

sentences.zh: 近長憲台，亦以剛直聞，是用委以機政，其益勉之！

translations.literal: Recently, as head of the Censorate, you are also known for firm uprightness; for this reason I entrust you with state affairs—redouble your efforts!"
translations.idiomatic: Since you recently headed the Censorate and are known for your uncompromising integrity, I am entrusting you with core state affairs. Apply yourself all the more!"

sentences.zh: 」未幾，進拜左丞。

translations.literal: " Not long after, he was further promoted to Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon afterward he was promoted to Left Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 襄在外任，治有異效，至是朝廷以褒賞廉吏詔天下，列其名以示獎勵。

translations.literal: When Xiang served in external posts, his governance had remarkable results; at this time the court issued a proclamation throughout the realm praising upright officials, listing his name to show encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: While serving in provincial posts, Xiang had achieved outstanding results. The court now issued a nationwide edict honoring upright officials and named him among them as an example.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，進拜平章政事，封蕭國公。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, he was further promoted to Grand Councilor and enfeoffed as Duke of Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year he was promoted to Grand Councilor and enfeoffed as Duke of Xiao.

sentences.zh: 世宗以金源郡王世嫡皇孫，將加王爵，詔擇國號。

translations.literal: Shizong, as the principal imperial grandson of the Prince of Jinyuan, was about to be granted princely rank, and an edict was issued to select a state name.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong, the principal imperial grandson of the Prince of Jinyuan, was to receive a princely title, and the court ordered a state name chosen for the enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 襄曰：「為天下大計，必先正其本，原者本也，請封原。

translations.literal: Xiang said: "For the great plan of the realm, one must first set right the root; yuan means root—I request enfeoffment as Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang said, "For the good of the empire we must first fix what is fundamental. Yuan means root—I propose the title Yuan.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " The proposal was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 故事，諸部族節度使及其僚屬多用颭人，而頗有私縱不法者，議改用諸色人。

translations.literal: By precedent, military commissioners of various tribal departments and their subordinates often employed Khitan, and there were many who privately indulged unlawful conduct; discussion turned to replacing them with people of various other categories.
translations.idiomatic: By custom, commissioners of the tribal departments and their staffs often used Khitan, many of whom had abused their positions. Officials debated replacing them with men of other backgrounds.

sentences.zh: 襄曰：「北邊雖無事，恆須經略之，若杜此門，其後有勞績，何以處之？

translations.literal: Xiang said: "Though the northern frontier is presently quiet, one must always manage it strategically; if this path is closed off, when someone later achieves merit, how will he be placed?
translations.idiomatic: Xiang said, "Even when the north is quiet we must still cultivate frontier talent. Close this avenue of advancement and we will have nowhere to reward future merit.

sentences.zh: 請如舊。

translations.literal: I request keeping the former practice.
translations.idiomatic: Let the old practice stand.

sentences.zh: 」他日，議及古有監軍之事。

translations.literal: " On another day, discussion turned to the ancient practice of army supervisors.
translations.idiomatic: " On another occasion the court discussed the old institution of army supervisors.

sentences.zh: 襄曰：「漢、唐初無監軍，將得專任，故戰必勝，攻必克。

translations.literal: Xiang said: "In early Han and Tang there were no army supervisors; generals had full authority, hence in battle they always won and in attack they always prevailed.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang said, "Early Han and Tang had no army supervisors. Generals held full command, so they fought to victory and stormed to success.

sentences.zh: 及叔世始以內臣監其軍，動為所制，故多敗而少功。

translations.literal: In later ages palace officials began to supervise armies and generals were constantly constrained by them, hence many defeats and few achievements.
translations.idiomatic: Only in decadent times did inner-court officials begin supervising armies, tying the generals' hands and producing more defeats than victories.

sentences.zh: 若將得其人，監軍誠不必置。

translations.literal: If the right general is obtained, supervisors truly need not be appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Appoint the right commander and there is no need for supervisors at all.

sentences.zh: 」並嘉納之。

translations.literal: " Both suggestions were approved and adopted.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor approved both recommendations.

sentences.zh: 詔受北部進貢。

translations.literal: An edict was issued for him to receive tribute from the northern regions.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to receive tribute from the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 使還，世宗問邊事，具圖以進，因上羈縻屬部、鎮服大石之策，詔悉行之。

translations.literal: When the envoy returned, Shizong asked about border affairs; he submitted detailed maps, and presented strategies for keeping subordinate tribes in submission and pacifying Dashi; an edict ordered all to be implemented.
translations.idiomatic: On his return Shizong questioned him about frontier affairs. Xiang submitted detailed maps and proposed policies to keep dependent tribes loyal and to subdue Dashi of the Qara Khitai. The emperor ordered all of it carried out.

sentences.zh: 進拜右丞相，徙封戴。

translations.literal: He was further promoted to Right Chancellor and transferred his fief to Dai.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Chancellor and his fief was changed to Dai.

sentences.zh: 世宗不豫，與太尉徒單克甯、平章政事張汝霖宿內殿，同受顧命。

translations.literal: When Shizong fell ill, together with Grand Commandant Tudan Kening and Grand Councilor Zhang Rulin he lodged in the inner hall and jointly received the final imperial charge.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong fell ill, Xiang stayed in the inner hall with Grand Commandant Tudan Kening and Grand Councilor Zhang Rulin and together received the emperor's deathbed charge.

sentences.zh: 章宗初即政，議罷僧道奴婢。

translations.literal: When Zhangzong first took power, discussion arose about abolishing the slave attendants of Buddhist and Daoist clergy.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after Zhangzong ascended the throne, the court debated abolishing the household slaves held by Buddhist and Daoist clergy.

sentences.zh: 太尉克甯奏曰：「此蓋成俗日久，若遽更之，於人情不安。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Kening memorialized: "This has surely been custom for a long time; if changed abruptly, people's feelings would be unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Kening argued, "This practice is deeply entrenched. To abolish it at once would unsettle public sentiment.

sentences.zh: 陛下如惡其數多，宜嚴立格法，以防濫度，則自少矣。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty dislikes their great number, strict regulations should be established to guard against indiscriminate ordination, and they would naturally diminish.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty finds their numbers excessive, set strict rules against indiscriminate ordination and the problem will shrink on its own.

sentences.zh: 」襄曰：「出家之人安用僕隸？

translations.literal: " Xiang said: "Why should those who leave home need servants?
translations.idiomatic: " Xiang replied, "What need have renunciants for servants?

sentences.zh: 乞不問從初如何所得，悉放為良。

translations.literal: I ask that regardless of how they were originally obtained, all be released as commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Regardless of how they were acquired, release them all as free commoners.

sentences.zh: 若寺觀物力元系奴婢之數推定者，併合除免。

translations.literal: If monasteries and temples had their property and resources calculated on the basis of slave numbers, let that too be abolished together.
translations.idiomatic: Any temple endowment calculated from slave quotas should be abolished as well.

sentences.zh: 」詔從襄言。

translations.literal: " An edict followed Xiang's view.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor issued an edict adopting Xiang's proposal.

sentences.zh: 由是二稅戶多為良者。

translations.literal: Thereupon many secondary tax households became commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Many secondary tax households were thereby made free commoners.

sentences.zh: 未幾，遣西北路招討使完顏安國等趨多泉子。

translations.literal: Not long after, Northwest Circuit Pacification Commissioner Wanyan Anguo and others were dispatched toward Duoquanzi.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Wanyan Anguo, Pacification Commissioner of the Northwest Circuit, and others were sent toward Duoquanzi.

sentences.zh: 密詔進討，乃命支軍出東道，襄由西道。

translations.literal: A secret edict ordered an advance punitive campaign; a branch army was ordered out by the eastern route while Xiang went by the western route.
translations.idiomatic: A secret edict ordered a punitive advance. A detached force marched by the eastern route while Xiang took the western route.

sentences.zh: 而東軍至龍駒河為阻珝所圍，三日不得出，求援甚急，或請俟諸軍集乃發。

translations.literal: But the eastern army reached Longju River and was besieged by Beizu Xu; for three days they could not break out and urgently sought relief; some urged waiting until all armies assembled before setting out.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern force reached the Longju River and was surrounded by Beizu Xu. Trapped for three days, it sent urgent appeals for help. Some urged Xiang to wait until the full army had gathered.

sentences.zh: 襄曰：「我軍被圍數日，馳救之猶恐不及，豈可後時？

translations.literal: Xiang said: "Our army has been besieged for days—even racing to save them I fear we may be too late; how can we delay?
translations.idiomatic: Xiang said, "Our men have been trapped for days. Even if we ride hard we may arrive too late—how can we wait?

sentences.zh: 」即鳴鼓夜發。

translations.literal: " Immediately drums were sounded and they set out at night.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered the drums beaten and marched that very night.

sentences.zh: 或請先遣人報圍中，使知援至。

translations.literal: Some urged first sending someone to notify those besieged so they would know relief had arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Others suggested sending a messenger ahead to tell the besieged troops that relief was coming.

sentences.zh: 襄曰：「所遣者儻為敵得，使知我兵寡而糧在後，則吾事敗矣。

translations.literal: Xiang said: "If the messenger sent is captured by the enemy and they learn our forces are few with grain still behind, our affair will fail.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang said, "If the enemy captures our messenger and learns how few we are—and that our supplies are still behind us—everything is lost.

sentences.zh: 」乃益疾馳。

translations.literal: " Thereupon they pressed on even more swiftly.
translations.idiomatic: " He pressed the march all the harder.

sentences.zh: 遲明，距敵近，眾請少憩。

translations.literal: At daybreak they were near the enemy; the troops asked for a brief rest.
translations.idiomatic: Near dawn they drew close to the enemy, and the men asked for a short rest.

sentences.zh: 襄曰：「吾所以乘夜疾馳者，欲掩其不備爾。

translations.literal: Xiang said: "The reason I drove through the night was to catch them unprepared.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang said, "We rode through the night to take them by surprise.

sentences.zh: 緩則不及。

translations.literal: If we slow down we will not make it in time.
translations.idiomatic: Hesitate now and we miss our chance.

sentences.zh: 」向晨壓敵，突擊之，圍中將士亦鼓噪出，大戰，獲輿帳牛羊。

translations.literal: " At dawn they pressed the enemy and charged them; the besieged officers and soldiers also rallied out with drum and shout; a great battle ensued and they captured carts, tents, cattle, and sheep.
translations.idiomatic: " At first light he closed on the enemy and struck. The trapped garrison burst out with shouts and drums. In the fierce battle they seized wagons, tents, cattle, and sheep.

sentences.zh: 眾皆奔斡里劄河。

translations.literal: The enemy all fled toward the Wenlizha River.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy fled toward the Wenlizha River.

sentences.zh: 遣安國追躡之。

translations.literal: Anguo was dispatched to pursue them.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang sent Anguo in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 眾散走，會大雨，凍死者十八九，降其部長，遂勒勳九峰石壁。

translations.literal: The troops scattered in flight; a heavy rain came and eight or nine out of ten died from exposure; their tribal chiefs submitted and merit was inscribed on the Nine Peaks stone cliff.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy scattered. A downpour followed, and eight or nine in ten died of exposure. Their chiefs surrendered, and the victory was carved on the stone cliff at Nine Peaks.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，上遣使厚賜以勞之，別詔許便宜賞賚士卒。

translations.literal: When victory was reported, the emperor sent envoys with generous rewards to commend them; a separate edict permitted discretionary reward of the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: When news of the victory arrived, the emperor sent envoys with rich rewards. A separate edict authorized Xiang to reward the troops at his discretion.

sentences.zh: 九月，赴闕，拜左丞相，監修國史，封常山郡王。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he went to court, was appointed Left Chancellor, Supervisor of the National History, and enfeoffed as Prince of Changshan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he returned to court, was made Left Chancellor and Supervisor of the National History, and enfeoffed as Prince of Changshan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 宴慶和殿，上親舉酒飲，解所服玉具佩刀以賜，俾即服之。

translations.literal: At a banquet in Qinghe Hall, the emperor personally raised a cup for him to drink, removed the jade-mounted sword at his waist and granted it, ordering him to put it on at once.
translations.idiomatic: At a banquet in Qinghe Hall the emperor personally offered him wine, took the jade-mounted sword from his own belt and gave it to him, and told him to wear it immediately.

sentences.zh: 十月，阻珝複叛，襄出屯北京，會群牧契丹德壽、陀鎖等據信州叛，偽建元曰身聖，眾號數十萬，遠近震駭。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Beizu Xu rebelled again; Xiang went out to encamp at Beijing; meanwhile the herding-office Khitan Deshou, Tuosuo, and others seized Xizhou in rebellion, falsely establishing an era title called Shengsheng, claiming hundreds of thousands of followers, and all near and far were shaken.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Beizu Xu rebelled again, and Xiang marched out to encamp at Beijing. At the same time the Khitan herding-office leaders Deshou and Tuosuo seized Xizhou, declared a reign title of Shengsheng, and claimed an army of hundreds of thousands, throwing the region into alarm.

sentences.zh: 襄閒暇如平日，人心乃安。

translations.literal: Xiang remained as leisurely as on ordinary days, and people's hearts then settled.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang remained as calm as on an ordinary day, and public morale steadied.

sentences.zh: 初，襄之出鎮也，至石門鎮，密謂僚屬曰：「北部犯塞奚足慮。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Xiang went out to take command, arriving at Shimen Town he secretly told his staff: "Northern border incursions are hardly worth worrying about.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiang first set out to take command, he reached Shimen Town and told his staff in confidence, "Raids from the northern frontier are nothing to fear.

sentences.zh: 第恐奸人乘隙而動。

translations.literal: I only fear treacherous men seizing the opportunity to act.
translations.idiomatic: What I fear is treacherous men exploiting the moment to rise.

sentences.zh: 北京近地軍少，當預為之備。

translations.literal: Beijing is nearby with few troops—a defense should be prepared in advance.
translations.idiomatic: Beijing is close at hand and thinly garrisoned. We must prepare in advance.

sentences.zh: 」即遣官發上京等軍六千，至是果得其用。

translations.literal: " He immediately dispatched officials to mobilize six thousand troops from Shangjing and elsewhere; at this juncture they proved useful indeed.
translations.idiomatic: " He immediately ordered officials to mobilize six thousand troops from Shangjing and elsewhere. When the crisis came, those men proved indispensable.

sentences.zh: 臨潢總管烏古論道遠、咸平總管蒲察守純分道進討，擒德壽等送京師。

translations.literal: Linhuang Circuit Administrator Wugulun Daoyuan and Xianping Circuit Administrator Pucha Shouchun advanced by separate routes and captured Deshou and others, sending them to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Wugulun Daoyuan, Administrator of Linhuang Circuit, and Pucha Shouchun, Administrator of Xianping Circuit, advanced on separate routes, captured Deshou and his fellows, and sent them to the capital.

sentences.zh: 契丹之亂，廷臣議罷郊祀，又欲改用正月上辛，上遣使問之，對曰：」郊為重禮，且先期詔天下，又籓國已報表賀，今若中罷，何以副四方傾望之意？

translations.literal: During the Khitan rebellion, court ministers discussed canceling the suburban sacrifice and also wanted to change to the first xin day of the first month; the emperor sent a messenger to ask him; he replied: "The suburban sacrifice is a weighty rite; moreover an edict has already gone out to the realm beforehand, and the frontier states have already submitted congratulatory memorials—if canceled midway now, how can we meet the expectant hopes of the four directions?
translations.idiomatic: During the Khitan uprising some ministers proposed canceling the suburban sacrifice or moving it to the first xin day of the first month. The emperor sent to ask Xiang's view. He replied, "The suburban sacrifice is a supreme rite. Edicts have already gone out to the empire, and the tributary states have sent congratulatory memorials. To halt it now would betray the expectations of the realm.

sentences.zh: 若改用正月上辛，乃祈穀之禮，非郊見上帝之本意也。

translations.literal: If changed to the first xin day of the first month, that is the grain-prayer rite, not the original intent of the suburban audience with Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The first xin day of the first month is the grain-prayer ceremony, not the true suburban audience with Heaven.

sentences.zh: 大禮不可輕廢，請決行之，臣乞於祀前滅賊。

translations.literal: A great rite must not be lightly abandoned; I ask that it be firmly carried out—I beg to destroy the rebels before the sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Such a great rite must not be cast aside lightly. Hold it as planned—I ask only to destroy the rebels before the ceremony.

sentences.zh: 」既而賊破，果如所料。

translations.literal: " Before long the rebels were broken, exactly as he had foreseen.
translations.idiomatic: " Before long the rebels were crushed, just as he had predicted.

sentences.zh: 郊禮成，進封南陽郡王。

translations.literal: When the suburban rite was completed, he was further enfeoffed as Prince of Nanyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After the suburban rite was completed, he was further enfeoffed as Prince of Nanyang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 始討契丹，自龍虎衛上將軍、節度使以下許承制授之。

translations.literal: At the start of the campaign against the Khitan, from Tiger-Dragon Guard Senior General and military commissioner downward, discretionary appointment was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: At the outset of the Khitan campaign, Xiang was authorized to appoint officers from Tiger-Dragon Guard Senior General and military commissioner downward at his discretion.

sentences.zh: 襄以為賞罰之柄非人臣所預，不敢奉詔。

translations.literal: Xiang held that the power of reward and punishment was not for a subject to hold and dared not accept the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang held that the power to reward and punish was not a minister's to wield and declined the commission.

sentences.zh: 賊平，請委近臣諭旨將士，使知上恩。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified, he asked that close ministers be entrusted to convey the imperial will to officers and soldiers so they would know the emperor's grace.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels were suppressed he asked that imperial envoys announce the emperor's will to the troops so they would know the throne's favor.

sentences.zh: 乃遣李仁惠持宣三十、敕百五十，視功給之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Li Renhui was sent carrying thirty proclamations and a hundred fifty edicts, distributing them according to merit.
translations.idiomatic: Li Renhui was then dispatched with thirty imperial proclamations and a hundred fifty edicts to distribute rewards according to merit.

sentences.zh: 方德壽之叛，諸颭亦剽略為民患，襄慮其與之合，乃移諸颭居之近京地，撫慰之。

translations.literal: When Deshou rebelled, various Khitan also raided and plundered to the people's harm; Xiang feared they would join him and therefore relocated various Khitan to settle near the capital and comforted them.
translations.idiomatic: While Deshou was in revolt, other Khitan bands were raiding the countryside. Fearing they would join the rebels, Xiang resettled Khitan groups near the capital and treated them with conciliation.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「颭人與北俗無異，今置內地，或生變奈何？

translations.literal: Someone said: "Khitan and northern customs are not different—placing them in the interior now, what if trouble arises?
translations.idiomatic: Someone objected, "The Khitan share the customs of the north. Move them into the interior and what if they turn against us?

sentences.zh: 」襄笑曰：「颭雖雜類，亦我之邊民，若撫以恩，焉能無感？

translations.literal: " Xiang smiled and said: "Though the Khitan are of mixed stock, they are also our frontier people; if treated with kindness, how could they fail to be moved?
translations.idiomatic: " Xiang smiled and said, "The Khitan may be of mixed origin, but they are still our frontier subjects. Treat them with kindness and they will respond.

sentences.zh: 我在此，必不敢動。

translations.literal: While I am here, they certainly dare not stir.
translations.idiomatic: While I remain here, they will not dare move.

sentences.zh: 」後果無患。

translations.literal: " Afterwards indeed there was no trouble.
translations.idiomatic: " In the end there was no trouble.

sentences.zh: 尋詔參知政事裔代領其軍。

translations.literal: Soon an edict had Associate Administrator Yi take over command of his army.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the emperor ordered Associate Administrator Yi to assume command of his army.

sentences.zh: 入見，賜錢五千萬。

translations.literal: He entered audience and was granted fifty million in cash.
translations.idiomatic: When he came to audience he was granted fifty million in cash.

sentences.zh: 明年，以內艱免。

translations.literal: The next year he was exempted from office due to mourning for a parent within the prescribed degrees.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he left office to observe mourning for a close relative.

sentences.zh: 翌日，起複視事。

translations.literal: The next day he was recalled from mourning to resume duties.
translations.idiomatic: The very next day he was recalled from mourning to resume his post.

sentences.zh: 時議以契丹戶之驅奴尚眾，乞盡鬻以散其黨，襄以為非便，奏請量存口數，餘悉官贖為良，上納之。

translations.literal: At the time opinion held that Khitan households still had many bonded attendants and asked that all be sold off to break up their factions; Xiang thought this inadvisable and memorialized requesting that household quotas be preserved while the remainder be redeemed by the state as commoners; the emperor accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Some argued that Khitan households still held large numbers of dependent slaves and urged selling them off to break rebel networks. Xiang disagreed and memorialized that fixed household quotas be preserved while the rest were redeemed by the state as free commoners. The emperor accepted.

sentences.zh: 北部複叛，裔戰失律，複命襄為左副元帥蒞師，尋拜樞密使兼平章政事，屯北京。

translations.literal: The northern regions rebelled again; Yi lost discipline in battle; Xiang was again appointed Left Deputy Commander-in-Chief to take command of the army, soon made Commissioner of Military Affairs concurrently Grand Councilor, encamped at Beijing.
translations.idiomatic: When the north rebelled again and Yi failed in battle, Xiang was again named Left Deputy Commander-in-Chief to take the field. He was soon made Commissioner of Military Affairs and Grand Councilor concurrently, and encamped at Beijing.

sentences.zh: 民方艱食，乃減價出糶倉粟以濟之。

translations.literal: The people were then suffering food shortage; he therefore sold grain from storehouses at reduced price to relieve them.
translations.idiomatic: The people were going hungry, so he sold grain from the state granaries at reduced prices to relieve them.

sentences.zh: 或以兵食方闕為言，襄曰：「烏有民足而兵不足者？

translations.literal: Some spoke of military provisions being scarce; Xiang said: "How can there be sufficient people yet insufficient soldiers?
translations.idiomatic: When some warned that army rations were already low, Xiang replied, "If the people are provided for, how can the army be wanting?

sentences.zh: 」卒行之，民皆悅服。

translations.literal: " In the end he carried it out and the people all submitted gladly.
translations.idiomatic: " He carried out the policy anyway, and the people submitted willingly.

sentences.zh: 時議北討，襄奏遣同判大睦親府事宗浩出軍泰州，又請左丞衡於撫州行樞密院，出軍西北路以邀阻珝，而自帥兵出臨潢。

translations.literal: At the time northern campaigning was discussed; Xiang memorialized dispatching Tongpan of the Great Closer-of-Kin Office Zonghao to lead troops from Taizhou, also requesting Left Vice Minister Heng establish a mobile Military Affairs Commission at Fuzhou to lead Northwest Circuit troops to intercept Beizu Xu, while he himself would lead troops out from Linhuang.
translations.idiomatic: As a northern campaign was debated, Xiang proposed sending Zonghao, Deputy Director of the Great Closer-of-Kin Office, to lead troops from Taizhou; sending Left Vice Minister Heng to establish a mobile Military Affairs Commission at Fuzhou to march Northwest Circuit forces against Beizu Xu; and leading his own army out from Linhuang.

sentences.zh: 上從其策，賜內庫物即軍中用之。

translations.literal: The emperor adopted his plan and granted inner-palace goods for immediate use in the army.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his plan and granted goods from the inner treasury for use in the field.

sentences.zh: 其後斜出部族詣撫州降，上專使問襄，襄以為受之便。

translations.literal: Afterwards the Xiechu tribe came to Fuzhou to submit; the emperor sent a special envoy to ask Xiang, and Xiang held accepting them advantageous.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Xiechu tribe came to Fuzhou to surrender. The emperor sent a special envoy to ask Xiang's view, and Xiang advised accepting them.

sentences.zh: 賜寶劍，詔度宜窮討。

translations.literal: He was granted a precious sword; an edict ordered him to pursue the enemy to the full as he saw fit.
translations.idiomatic: He received an imperial sword and an edict authorizing him to pursue the enemy as far as he judged necessary.

sentences.zh: 乃令士自齎糧以省挽運，進屯於沔移剌烈、烏滿掃等山以逼之。

translations.literal: He then ordered soldiers to carry their own grain to save on transport and advanced to encamp at Gan Yila Lie, Wumansao, and other mountains to press the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the troops to carry their own rations to reduce supply trains and advanced to encamp on Gan Yila Lie, Wumansao, and neighboring heights to press the enemy.

sentences.zh: 因請就用步卒穿壕築障，起臨潢左界北京路以為阻塞。

translations.literal: He also requested using infantry to dig trenches and build barriers from the left border of Linhuang through the Beijing Circuit as a blockade.
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed deploying infantry to dig trenches and build barriers from the Linhuang frontier through Beijing Circuit as a blocking line.

sentences.zh: 言者多異同，詔問方略。

translations.literal: Many opinions differed; an edict asked for his strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Opinion in court was divided, and the emperor asked for his strategic assessment.

sentences.zh: 襄曰：「今茲之費雖百萬貫，然功一成則邊防固而戍兵可減半，歲省三百萬貫，且寬民轉輸之力，實為永利。

translations.literal: Xiang said: "Though this year's expense is a million strings of cash, once the work is done the frontier defenses will be solid and garrison troops can be halved, saving three million strings annually, and easing the people's burden of transport—it is truly lasting benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang said, "This project will cost a million strings of cash, but once finished the frontier will be secure, garrison strength can be cut in half, and three million strings will be saved each year while easing the people's transport burden. The long-term gain is clear.

sentences.zh: 」詔可。

translations.literal: " The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 襄親督視之，軍民並役，又募饑民以傭即事，五旬而畢。

translations.literal: Xiang personally supervised it; soldiers and civilians worked together, and hungry people were also recruited as hired labor; it was completed in fifty days.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang personally oversaw the work. Soldiers and civilians labored together, and hungry locals were hired as laborers. The project was finished in fifty days.

sentences.zh: 於是西北、西南路亦治塞如所請。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Northwest and Southwest circuits also fortified frontier defenses as requested.
translations.idiomatic: The Northwest and Southwest circuits then built frontier defenses along the same lines.

sentences.zh: 無何，泰州軍與敵接戰，宗浩督其後，殺獲過半，諸部相率送款，襄納之。

translations.literal: Before long the Taizhou army engaged the enemy in battle; Zonghao commanded the rear and killed and captured more than half; the various tribes submitted one after another, and Xiang accepted them.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Taizhou army met the enemy in battle. Zonghao commanded the rear guard and killed or captured more than half the foe. One tribe after another submitted, and Xiang accepted their surrender.

sentences.zh: 自是北陲遂定。

translations.literal: From then on the northern frontier was settled.
translations.idiomatic: From that point the northern frontier was pacified.

sentences.zh: 襄還臨潢，減屯兵四萬、馬二萬疋。

translations.literal: Xiang returned to Linhuang and reduced stationed troops by forty thousand and horses by twenty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang returned to Linhuang and cut stationed forces by forty thousand men and twenty thousand horses.

sentences.zh: 上以信符召還，遣近臣迎勞於途。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned him back with a tally-token and sent close ministers to welcome and commend him on the road.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor recalled him with an imperial tally and sent close ministers to welcome and honor him on the road.

sentences.zh: 既至，複撫問於第，入獻邊機十事，皆為施行，仍厚賜之，複拜左丞相。

translations.literal: Once arrived, the emperor again comforted and inquired at his residence; he entered and presented ten items of frontier strategy, all of which were implemented; he was again generously rewarded and reappointed Left Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: On his arrival the emperor visited his residence to inquire after him. Xiang presented ten proposals on frontier affairs, all of which were adopted. He was richly rewarded and reappointed Left Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 初，襄至自軍，上諭宰臣曰：「樞密使襄築立邊堡完固。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Xiang arrived from the army, the emperor told the chief ministers: "Commissioner of Military Affairs Xiang has built frontier fortifications that are complete and solid.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiang first returned from campaign, the emperor told his chief ministers, "Commissioner of Military Affairs Xiang has built frontier fortifications that are complete and strong.

sentences.zh: 古來立一城一邑，尚有賞賚，即欲拜三公，三公非賞功官，如左丞相亦非賞功者，雖然可特授之。

translations.literal: Since ancient times even establishing one city or one town still brought reward; I wish immediately to appoint him Three Excellencies—but the Three Excellencies are not reward-for-merit offices, and likewise Left Chancellor is not a reward office; even so, it may be specially conferred.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity even the founding of a single town brought reward. I would promote him at once to the Three Excellencies—but those are not mere merit titles, and neither is Left Chancellor. Even so, an extraordinary appointment is warranted.

sentences.zh: 」遣左司郎中阿勒根阿海降詔褒諭。

translations.literal: " Left Department Director Aleigen Ahai was sent down with an edict of praise and instruction.
translations.idiomatic: " He sent Left Department Director Aleigen Ahai with an edict of commendation.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，進拜司空，領左丞相如故。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year he was further promoted to Minister of Works while retaining Left Chancellor as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year he was promoted to Minister of Works while continuing as Left Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 襄重厚寡言，務以鎮靜守法。

translations.literal: Xiang was grave, steady, and sparing of speech, striving through calm steadfastness to uphold the law.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang was grave and taciturn, relying on calm restraint and strict adherence to law.

sentences.zh: 每掾有所稟，必問曰：「諸相雲何？

translations.literal: Whenever a clerk had something to report, he always asked: "What do the other chancellors say?
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a clerk brought him a matter, he always asked first, "What do the other chancellors say?

sentences.zh: 」掾對某相如是，某相如是。

translations.literal: " The clerk would answer that one chancellor said thus and another said thus.
translations.idiomatic: " The clerk would report what each chancellor had said.

sentences.zh: 襄曰：「從某議。

translations.literal: Xiang said: "Follow so-and-so's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang would say, "Follow that chancellor's view.

sentences.zh: 」其事無有異者。

translations.literal: " In these matters there was nothing different.
translations.idiomatic: " In such cases he never acted otherwise.

sentences.zh: 識者謂襄誠得相體。

translations.literal: Those with discernment said Xiang truly grasped the proper bearing of a chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Those who knew him well said Xiang truly had the temperament of a chancellor.

sentences.zh: 時上頗更定制度，初置提刑司，又議設清閒職位，如宋朝宮觀使，以待年高致仕之官。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor was considerably revising institutions, first establishing the Office of Judicial Inspection, and also debating the creation of idle honorary posts, like the Song dynasty's Palace Attendant Commissioners, to accommodate officials who had retired on account of age.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then overhauling the institutions: he first established the Office of Judicial Inspection and also debated creating honorary sinecures, modeled on the Song dynasty's palace-attendant commissioners, for officials who had retired in old age.

sentences.zh: 襄言：「年老致仕，朝廷養以俸廩，恩禮至渥。

translations.literal: Xiang said: "When the aged retire, the court sustains them with salary and grain; the grace and courtesy are extremely generous.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang said, "When officials retire in old age, the court supports them with salary and provisions, and the grace shown them is already very great.

sentences.zh: 老不為退，複有省會之法，所以抑貪冒，長廉節。

translations.literal: For the aged who do not retire, there is also the provincial reporting system, by which greed and corruption are restrained and integrity is fostered.
translations.idiomatic: The requirement that the old not linger in office, together with the provincial reporting system, exists to check greed and foster integrity.

sentences.zh: 若擬別設，恐涉於濫。

translations.literal: If separate posts are proposed, I fear it will verge on excess.
translations.idiomatic: If we propose separate posts on top of that, I fear we will invite abuse.

sentences.zh: 」又言：「省事不如省官，今提刑官吏，多無益於治，徒亂有司事。

translations.literal: " He also said: "Cutting institutions is not as good as cutting officials. Today's judicial inspection officials mostly do not benefit governance and only disrupt the business of the regular authorities.
translations.idiomatic: " He also said, "It is better to reduce officials than to reduce institutions. Most of the officials in the judicial inspection offices do nothing for good governance and only interfere with the work of the regular offices.

sentences.zh: 議者以謂斯乃外台，不宜罷。

translations.literal: Those debating held that this was an external circuit office and should not be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Those in the debate argued that this was a circuit-level office and should not be abolished.

sentences.zh: 臣恐混淆之辭，徒煩聖聽。

translations.literal: Your servant fears this muddled talk merely burdens Your Majesty's ears.
translations.idiomatic: I fear this confused argument will only weary Your Majesty's attention to no purpose.

sentences.zh: 且憲台所掌者察官吏非違，正下民冤枉，亦無提點刑獄、舉薦之權。

translations.literal: Moreover, what the Censorate oversees is investigating officials' misconduct and correcting the wrongs of the common people; it has no authority to supervise criminal cases or make recommendations.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the Censorate's charge is to investigate official misconduct and redress the grievances of the people; it has no authority to oversee criminal trials or make recommendations.

sentences.zh: 若已設難以遽更，其採訪廉能不宜隸本司，宜令監察御史歲終體究，仍不時選官廉訪。

translations.literal: If what has been established cannot be quickly changed, the inquiry into integrity and capability should not be subordinated to this office; it should be entrusted to the Investigating Censors for thorough examination at year's end, and officials should still be selected from time to time for integrity inspections.
translations.idiomatic: If the new office cannot be abolished at once, then the search for upright and capable men should not be placed under it. Instead, Investigating Censors should conduct a full review at year's end, and officials should still be chosen from time to time for integrity tours.

sentences.zh: 」上皆聽納。

translations.literal: " The emperor accepted all of it.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor accepted all his recommendations.

sentences.zh: 俄乞致仕，不許。

translations.literal: Soon he requested retirement; it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he asked to retire, but the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 時方旱，命有司祈雨，襄及平章政事張萬公、參政僕散揆等上表待罪。

translations.literal: Drought had set in; the court ordered the relevant offices to pray for rain. Xiang, together with Grand Chancellor Zhang Wannu, Vice Grand Chancellor Pusan Kui, and others submitted memorials accepting blame.
translations.idiomatic: A drought was then afflicting the realm. The court ordered the relevant offices to pray for rain, and Xiang, together with Grand Chancellor Zhang Wannu, Vice Grand Chancellor Pusan Kui, and others submitted memorials accepting blame.

sentences.zh: 上召翰林學士党懷英草罪己詔，仍慰諭襄等視事。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Hanlin Academician Dang Huaiying to draft a self-reproach edict, and still comforted and instructed Xiang and the others to continue their duties.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Hanlin Academician Dang Huaiying to draft an edict of self-reproach, but still comforted Xiang and the others and told them to remain at their posts.

sentences.zh: 泰和元年春，承命馳禱於亳州太清宮及後土方嶽。

translations.literal: In the spring of the first year of Taihe, he received orders and hastened to pray at the Taiqing Palace in Bozhou and at the terrestrial spirit mountains of the four directions.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the first year of Taihe, he received orders and hastened to offer prayers at the Taiqing Palace in Bozhou and at the sacred mountains of earth.

sentences.zh: 以其世封遠，特改授河間府路算術海猛安。

translations.literal: Because his hereditary fief was far away, he was specially reassigned to Suanshu Hai of Hejian Prefecture Circuit as meng'an.
translations.idiomatic: Because his hereditary fief lay far away, he was specially reassigned to Suanshu Hai in Hejian Prefecture Circuit as meng'an.

sentences.zh: 明年，皇子生，襄複自請報謝。

translations.literal: The next year, when a prince was born, Xiang again volunteered to offer thanks on the court's behalf.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, when a prince was born, Xiang again volunteered to go and offer thanks on the court's behalf.

sentences.zh: 既祀嵩嶽，還次芝田之府店，遂以疾薨，年六十三。

translations.literal: After sacrificing at Mount Song, he stopped at the postal station at Zhitian on the return journey and there died of illness, aged sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: After performing the rites at Mount Song, he halted at the postal station at Zhitian on the return journey and there died of illness, aged sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 訃聞，輟朝，遣使祭于路，葬禮依太師淄王克寧。

translations.literal: When word of his death arrived, court was suspended; envoys were sent to offer sacrifices on the road; funeral rites followed those of Grand Preceptor Prince Zi of Linzi, Kening.
translations.idiomatic: When word of his death arrived, court was suspended. Envoys were sent to offer sacrifices along the road, and his funeral followed the precedent set for Grand Preceptor Prince Zi of Linzi, Kening.

sentences.zh: 諡曰武昭。

translations.literal: Posthumous title: Wuzhao.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous title Wuzhao.

sentences.zh: 命張行簡銘其碑。

translations.literal: Zhang Xingjian was ordered to compose the inscription for his stele.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xingjian was ordered to inscribe his stele.

sentences.zh: 襄明敏，才武過人，上親待之厚，故所至有功。

translations.literal: Xiang was bright and keen, his martial talent surpassing others; the emperor personally treated him with great favor, and therefore wherever he went he achieved merit.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang was quick and perceptive, and his martial talent surpassed that of others. The emperor personally favored him deeply, and wherever he was sent he achieved results.

sentences.zh: 其駐軍臨潢也，有以偽書遺西京留守徒單鎰，欲構以罪。

translations.literal: When he was stationed at Linhuang, someone sent a forged letter to Western Capital Intendant Tudan Yi, seeking to frame him with a crime.
translations.idiomatic: While he was encamped at Linhuang, someone sent a forged letter to Western Capital Intendant Tudan Yi, hoping to frame him with a crime.

sentences.zh: 書聞，上以書還畀襄，其明信如此。

translations.literal: When the letter was reported, the emperor returned the letter to Xiang—such was the trust placed in him.
translations.idiomatic: When the letter came to light, the emperor returned it to Xiang. Such was the trust the throne placed in him.

sentences.zh: 既而果獲為偽書者。

translations.literal: Before long the forger was indeed captured.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the forger was indeed caught.

sentences.zh: 在政府二十年，明練故事，簡重能斷，器局尤寬大，待掾吏盡禮，用人各得所長，為當世名將相。

translations.literal: Twenty years in the central government; well versed in precedent; concise, grave, and decisive; his breadth of mind especially generous; he treated clerks with full courtesy; in employing men each was placed according to his strengths—a renowned general and minister of his age.
translations.idiomatic: He spent twenty years in the central government, thoroughly versed in precedent, concise and grave in manner, and decisive in judgment. His breadth of mind was especially large: he treated clerks with full courtesy and placed each man where his strengths could serve. He was accounted one of the age's great generals and ministers.

sentences.zh: 大安間，配享章宗廟廷。

translations.literal: During the Da'an era, he was granted collateral sacrifice in Zhangzong's ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: During the Da'an era he was granted a place in collateral sacrifice in Zhangzong's ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 夾谷衡

translations.literal: Jiagu Heng
translations.idiomatic: Jiagu Heng

sentences.zh: 夾谷衡，本名阿里不，山東西路三土猛安益打把謀克人也。

translations.literal: Jiagu Heng, original name Alibu, was a man of the Sandu Meng'an Yida baimouke in Shandong West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Jiagu Heng, whose original name was Alibu, came from the Sandu Meng'an Yida baimouke in Shandong West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 大定十三年，創設女直進士舉，衡中第四人，補東平府教授。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Dading, when the Jurchen jinshi examination was first established, Heng placed fourth and was appointed professor at Dongping Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Dading, when the Jurchen jinshi examination was first instituted, Heng placed fourth and was appointed professor at Dongping Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 調范陽簿，選充國史院編修官，改應奉翰林文字。

translations.literal: Transferred to Fanyang assistant magistrate; selected as compiler in the National History Institute; changed to Hanlin text attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to assistant magistrate of Fanyang, selected as a compiler in the National History Institute, and then made a Hanlin text attendant.

sentences.zh: 世宗嘗謂宰臣曰：「女直進士中才傑之士蓋亦難得，如徒單鎰、夾穀衡、尼龐古鑒，皆有用材也。
